shortDescription: Run the AIX iostat command to monitor system I/O statistics.

options.name: adapter_report
options.description: Display the adapter throughput report (-a).

options.name: block_io
options.description: Displays the block I/O device utilization statistics. The -b flag is mutually exclusive to all flags, except the -T flag.

options.name: concatenated_output
options.description: Controls whether the output of the iostat command is appended to the output file or is overwrited. If set to true, output will be appended to the file. If set to false, the file will be overwritten with fresh output.

options.name: count
options.description: The Count parameter can be specified in conjunction with the Interval parameter. If the Count parameter is specified, the value of count determines the number of reports generated at Interval seconds apart. If the 'count' is not mentioned with the 'interval' option, then the default value of 5 will be considered.

options.name: drives
options.description: List of drives to include in the report.

options.name: extended_drive
options.description: Display extended tape/drive utilization.

options.name: filesystems
options.description: List of file filesystem to be used.

options.name: fs_only
options.description: Displays the file system utilization report, and turns off other utilization reports..

options.name: fs_utilization
options.description: Display file system utilization (-f).

options.name: interval
options.description: Parameter specifies the amount of time in seconds between each report. If the Interval parameter is not specified, the iostat command generates a single report containing statistics for the time since system startup (boot).

options.name: long_list
options.description: Displays the output in long listing mode.

options.name: no_disk
options.description: Turns off the display of disk utilization report. The -t and -d flags together turn off both disks and TTY or CPU statistics, allowed only with the -a or -s flags

options.name: no_tty_cpu
options.description: Turns off the display of TTY utilization report or CPU utilization report. If you do not specify the -d or -p flag, then by default the -d flag is turned on. The -t and -d flags together turn off both disks and TTY or CPU statistics, allowed only with the -a or -s flags. The -d flag is mutually exclusive with the -t flag unless you specify the -a or -s flag, too. The -d flag is mutually exclusive with the -p flag unless you specify the -a or -s flag, too.

options.name: nonzero_stats
options.description: Display valid nonzero statistics.

options.name: options_override
options.description: Changes the content and presentation of the iostat report based on the values specified in option parameters.

options.name: path_utilization
options.description: Displays the path utilization report.

options.name: recorded_output
options.description: Path to file where command output should be written.

options.name: reset_ext_stats
options.description: Specifies that the reset of min* and max* values should happen at each interval. The default is to reset the values once when iostat is started. The -R flag can be specified only with the -D flag

options.name: reset_io
options.description: Resets the disk input/output statistics. Only root users can use this option.

options.name: scale_power
options.description: Displays the processor statistics that are multiplied by a value of 10power. The default value of the power parameter is 0

options.name: show_timestamp
options.description: Displays the time stamp.

options.name: system_throughput
options.description: Specifies the system throughput report. You can specify the -a flag with the -A flag, but not when you have specified the -q or -Q flag.

options.name: wpar_stats
options.description: Reports I/O activities of a workload partition. Specify -@ 'ALL' to display the activity for the global environment and all workload partitions in the system. Specify the -@ flag with a list of workload partition names to display the activity for that workload partition. Specify -@ 'Global' to display the activity for the global environment only. Specify the -@ flag inside a WPAR to display system-wide statistics along with WPAR statistics.

options.name: xml_output
options.description: Generates the XML output. The default file name is iostat_DDMMYYHHMM.xml unless you specify a different file name by using the -o option.

options.name: xml_output_path
options.description: Specifies the file name for the XML output.
